title: Gate an n8n news brief with Jev: three questions, one filter, visible failures
description: Filter a daily n8n news digest with three Jev questions per article, tune the thresholds from logged answers, and keep an outage from looking like a quiet day.

source.title: Build a morning AI news brief with You.com, Jev, and n8n

author.name: n8n team (guest post by Tyler Eastman, You.com)

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Original editorial guide; AI-assisted research, drafting and offline verification

image.alt: An n8n news brief in three stages: search wide and skip seen articles, ask Jev three questions per article and combine them in a filter, then route Jev errors to an alert instead of dropping them as noise

connections.why: The blog and library export use HTTP Request; the linked companion at 2359416 already uses TypeSafe Evaluate. The cataloged official node supports the same answers.<id>.noul/.score fields and an explicit error output. This remains an editorial connection because the blog does not name the package.
connections.limitations: MIT n8n community node; requires an n8n instance that can install community nodes and a TypeSafe API key, and live use is billed. Its error behaviour and output field names may differ from the HTTP Request version, so the filter expressions and the error branch must be re-checked after swapping. Source inspected; not installed or run. Install the scoped package @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai. Validate answer presence, numeric type and ranges before marking seen. Moving deduplication after judgment may repeat paid inference; it does not recover failed Research or Slack delivery.

Inspected library workflow 20558 through its public template API, and linked companion youdotcom-oss/n8n-ai-brief-workflow at 2359416d502a5e732df74a6e9be42c38b1d4b81d. Library uses HTTP Request; companion already uses TypeSafe Evaluate. Both retain early deduplication, three-answer filters and continueRegularOutput. verification.offline: Ran a Node.js 22 simulation of the template's filter expressions and node order with no n8n instance or network: three passing answers keep an article; a minor score or a low development probability drops it; an item carrying an error instead of answers is also dropped, because missing values default to 0. Because deduplication runs before the Jev call, an article seen during a Jev outage is not judged on the next run. In a variant that marks articles seen only after a successful answer and counts errors, the article is judged and posted the next day if search still returns it. Checked TypeSafe's models and pricing, Noul, Score and confidence docs. Audit replay added seven authored policy/bookkeeping assertions: valid, low score, provider error, missing, nonnumeric, out-of-range and repeated-valid responses. Invalid/error responses remain unseen in the proposed order. The normalized urlKey must come from the linked Prepare article item after the HTTP response. This does not exercise actual n8n item linking, persistent deduplication or delivery.

faqs.question: Why ask Jev three questions instead of one?
faqs.answer: Each question judges one thing, so you can see which one drifted and tune its threshold separately. The template asks whether an article reports a new development, whether it is about the topic, and how material it is to your team, in one request.

faqs.question: How much does the Jev filter cost per morning?
faqs.answer: The source estimates about $0.00004 per article and $0.01 to $0.04 for a whole morning, including You.com search and research. Check TypeSafe's current pricing and your own token counts before relying on that figure.

faqs.question: What does materialityThreshold 1.3 mean?
faqs.answer: The template's materiality Score has three levels numbered 0 to 2: noise, minor and material. The returned score is probability-weighted, so 1.3 keeps articles that lean towards material. Tune it from a week of logged scores.

faqs.question: Is Jev's answer here a calibrated confidence?
faqs.answer: Not by default. A Noul returns a probability of yes and has no separate confidence field, and a Score returns a weighted level. Whether 0.8 means 80 percent on your news feed is something to check against your own labels.

faqs.question: What happens if the Jev call fails?
faqs.answer: In the template as published, the Jev node continues on error and the filter treats missing answers as 0, so the article is dropped like noise and has already been marked as seen. Route errors to an alert so an outage does not look like a quiet day.

faqs.question: Do I need You.com to use this pattern?
faqs.answer: No. The gate works on any list of items with a title and description. You.com supplies search and the written brief in the template; any search source and any summariser can take those places.
